feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Iteration 4 (291.9) remains the reference. Iterations 5 (60 mm span), 6 (16 mm footprint) and 7 (wheel_track 0.10 m) each left the oval at 0 of 20 finishes, and line_loss_events stayed at 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom in every case. Iteration 7 is the key evidence against a narrower track: at 0.10 m, max_error rose to 0.065 to 0.070 and the oval lost all finishes, so turning authority via track width did not help. Your plan to restore wheel_track 0.12 m is correct. Sensing (span, footprint, forward position) and track width have now all been tried around the iteration-4 layout without clearing bend line loss. Mass 0.5 kg is the one remaining single-variable test, and it is reasonable to run it on the iteration-4 geometry. Next race: if the oval finish rate holds at or above 0.75 and line_loss_events falls on the s-bend or slalom, keep 0.5 kg and consider a modest further mass reduction. If the oval finish rate drops below 0.75 or the score falls below 291.9, return to the exact iteration-4 geometry at 0.6 kg. If line loss stays at 2.0 on the bends with mass 0.5 kg, stop searching sensor geometry and report that the limit is control response, since no geometry variant has cleared it.

If the score falls below 291.9 or the oval finish rate drops below 0.75, revert to mass 0.6 kg with the exact iteration-4 geometry, which is the best known design.

If line_loss_events stays at 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom after the mass change, stop geometry search and propose only controller-side tests, since span, footprint, forward position and track width have all been tried without clearing it.
